title: POC scoping - hosted vs dedicated vs private
next_steps: Maya to send pricing and POC statement of work by 2026-12-02
Carlos to share benchmark checklist and sample workloads by 2026-12-03
Veridian to provide sample dataset and expected QPS by 2026-12-04
Schedule 1-week hosted benchmark run starting week of 2026-12-07
action_items: Carlos Nguyen: Send benchmark guide, perf scripts, and infra checklist (due 2026-12-03)
Lena Ortiz (Veridian): Upload 2 sample datasets and traffic profile (due 2026-12-04)
Sophie Grant (Veridian Security): Confirm SOC2/SSO/KMS requirements and provide contacts (due 2026-12-06)
summary: AE + SE ran a POC scoping call with Veridian Health to align on success criteria (latency, accuracy, cost), workload sizing (QPS, tokens per request), benchmark approach, and timelines. Discussed tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and agreed next steps: run a 1-week hosted benchmark, share SOW/pricing, and collect sample datasets.
topics: Success criteria (latency p95, quality evals, cost targets)
Timeline and decision criteria for deployment mode
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we, we wanted to run through the POC scope for Veridian. Intro quick round robin please
[00:12] Rajiv (CTO): Hi Rajiv here, we run the infra and ML stack, we want to evaluate inference cost and latency for our clinical summarization use case
[00:22] Lena (MLOps): Lena here, I'll own the data side and run the traffic profiles for the benchmark
[00:28] Carlos (Redwood SE): Carlos, SE, I will lead benchmarks and perf tuning, happy to dig into batch sizes, quantization, kv cache etc
[00:36] Sophie (Security): Sophie, security and compliance, I'll be asking the SOC2/KMS questions
[00:44] Evan (PM): Evan product, timeline oriented
[00:48] Maya: Cool, quick agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, bench plan, hosted vs dedicated vs private decision factors, and next steps. Sound OK?
[00:57] Rajiv: Yep, go ahead
[01:02] Maya: First, success criteria — what does success look like for the POC?
[01:08] Rajiv: Primary is latency, we need p95 under 300ms for single-turn summarization at our median token length ~300 tokens, and throughput to handle bursts of 60 QPS sustained for 10 minutes. Secondary is inference cost — we want to understand cost per 1M tokens and unit economics. Third is quality: no regressions vs our current model, we'll run an eval set. Also security controls must be validated for enterprise usage.
[01:35] Carlos: Couple clarifying q's — when you say 300 tokens median, is that input only or input+output?
[01:41] Rajiv: input only, output typically 80–120 tokens
[01:46] Lena: Our traffic profile is 20 QPS baseline, bursts to 60 QPS, concurrency around 30–40. We'll upload a sample trace.
[01:54] Maya: Good, that gives us numbers to right-size. On deployment modes: quick primer — Hosted is fastest to start (we run the model in Redwood's hosted infra), Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale, Private (VPC/on-prem) is for strict data residency or air-gap. Tradeoffs are speed to start, cost, and control.
[02:18] Sophie: From security, private is ideal but also bigger project. We need SSO, RBAC, KMS integration and audit logs. Is the hosted option compatible with KMS?
[02:28] Carlos: Hosted supports customer-managed keys in some regions and we can provide audit logs; there are obviously limitations vs fully private where the control plane runs in your VPC. We have a SOC2 report we can share.
[02:40] Maya: Also note Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints for network isolation, it's often the middle ground.
[02:47] Rajiv: Good. For the POC we probably will test hosted first to get baseline numbers, and if latency/cost look promising, move to a dedicated pilot. If there's a hard compliance requirement we might go private later.
[02:58] Carlos: That is the standard path. For benchmarks we suggest a 1-week hosted run to collect p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost metrics, using your production trace. Then a dedicated sizing estimate and then a short dedicated pilot (1–2 weeks) if needed.
[03:14] Evan: What's typical timeline to get dedicated capacity?
[03:18] Maya: Usually 4–8 weeks depending on GPU type and SLAs; private deployments can be 8–16 weeks depending on on-prem procurement and network setup.
[03:27] Lena: For the hosted benchmark what artifacts do you need?
[03:31] Carlos: We'll need a sample dataset, a traffic profile (QPS over time), expected concurrency, and any accuracy eval set. Also a list of models you want to test and any prompt templates. We'll provide the perf harness and instructions.
[03:45] Rajiv: Model question — do you have models tuned for summarization? We saw 'Redwood-2' in docs — is that what you recommend?
[03:52] Maya: We have several variants; for summarization we recommend starting with rw-7b and a quantized 4-bit variant for cost testing, and a 13b variant for quality testing. We'll be explicit in the SOW.
[04:05] Carlos: Note that quantization and batching will change latency characteristics: batching improves throughput and cost but can increase tail latency. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and token-level cost to understand tradeoffs.
[04:18] Sophie: For encryption, we require KMS integration and customer-managed keys for at-rest. Can hosted fulfill that?
[04:25] Carlos: Hosted can integrate with customer KMS for certain regions — we'll include architecture notes, but private gives you the tightest control. We'll share our SOC2 and the encryption whitepaper.
[04:36] Maya: Let's talk metrics and success gates so there is no ambiguity — propose: p95 latency <300ms on median 380 tokens (input+output) for hosted baseline; cost target <= $X per 1M tokens (we'll compute once we know model variant); accuracy delta <1% on the evaluation metric; and security checklist items validated. Agree?
[04:56] Rajiv: That sounds reasonable, but we need to cap the allowable p99 — if p99 spikes above 1s during bursts that's a problem.
[05:04] Carlos: We'll measure p99 and surface distribution. For bursts, we'll test autoscale and warm pools (dedicated) and see how much warm capacity reduces p99.
[05:14] Lena: Regarding dataset, we have PHI-ish data, can we scrub or run with synthetic?
[05:19] Sophie: Security prefers synthetic for the hosted benchmark; we'll provide redacted/synth samples. If POC moves to dedicated or private then we can test with real data under NDA.
[05:30] Maya: Ok good. Bench plan: week 1 hosted smoke + baseline (3–4 days), week 2 sustained runs and edge cases, collect logs and metrics, then Redwood will produce a sizing + cost recommendation and a pilot plan for dedicated if needed.
[05:47] Evan: What's the instrumentation we get? Traces, per-route cost?
[05:51] Carlos: You'll get token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency, per-token timing, and error traces. We can integrate tracing hooks into your app if you want.
[06:02] Rajiv: One question — how do you handle model fallbacks? If we use a larger model for some reqs and cheaper model for others, do you route automatically?
[06:10] Maya: Smart routing is supported: policy-based routing by latency, cost, or model quality. We can set rules for fallbacks, and Redwood Optimize can suggest profiles.
[06:20] Rajiv: Competitors — we looked at OpenAI and Bedrock; any delta we should expect?
[06:25] Carlos: Bedrock and OpenAI are fine for hosted but Dedicated/private options and integration variety differ; we can run apples-to-apples benchmarks for you.
[06:33] Maya: Budget question — do you have a target spend for the pilot?
[06:36] Evan: We're budgeting a few thousand for initial POC, but need a clear estimate before sign-off.
[06:42] Maya: We'll provide rough cost estimates in the SOW and post-hosted benchmark we'll provide more accurate TCO.
[06:50] Lena: Any pitfalls you've seen?
[06:53] Carlos: Common issues: not providing realistic traffic traces, ignoring tail latencies, and underestimating cache/prefix reuse. Also tokenization differences between models can alter cost.
[07:06] Rajiv: About caching — do you support KV cache/prefix caching to reduce cost for repeated contexts?
[07:11] Carlos: Yes, Redwood runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; it can significantly help for chat-like workloads, less so for single-turn summarization. We'll test with and without cache.
[07:23] Sophie: Can we get a copy of the SOC2 and network architecture?
[07:27] Maya: Yes, we'll send SOC2, security whitepaper, and a network diagram.
[07:31] Evan: Ok next, decision criteria for hosted vs dedicated vs private — can you summarize recommended decision tree?
[07:39] Carlos: Sure: Start hosted if you want fastest time-to-value and no hard data residency need. If you need predictable throughput, lower unit cost at scale, and network isolation, choose Dedicated. If you have regulatory or air-gap requirements, choose Private. If security asserts need to see keys in your VPC, Private; if just KMS + peering, Dedicated often suffices.
[07:59] Rajiv: That matches our internal thinking. For SLA, do you offer uptime SLAs for Dedicated?
[08:04] Maya: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets as part of the contract. Hosted has standard availability but less guaranteed latency.
[08:12] Lena: For the dedicated sizing, how do you estimate GPU type?
[08:16] Carlos: We base it on model architecture, sequence length, concurrency, and desired latency SLO. We'll run the perf results from hosted to estimate GPU hours and recommended instance type (e.g., A100 vs H100 vs equivalent).
[08:29] Evan: Anything else on timeline?
[08:31] Maya: Next practical steps: we'll kick off hosted benchmark once Veridian provides datasets and traffic profile; Redwood sends SOW + pricing; conduct hosted run week of Dec 7; deliver results and dedicated sizing within 5 business days after run.
[08:47] Rajiv: Sounds good. One more security nit: we will need an architecture review with our InfoSec before any data lands on hosted.
[08:54] Sophie: yes, we'll schedule an architecture review with Redwood security folks if needed.
[08:59] Maya: Perfect — I'll capture action items. Thanks everyone.
[09:04] Carlos: I'll follow up with the perf scripts and a short README. Benchmark spreadsheet link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/veridian (placeholder)
[09:15] Evan: Great, thanks all
[09:18] Rajiv: Thanks
[09:20] End of recording

Notes on transcription: minor mis-hearings and truncated words present (e.g., "kv cache" sometimes transcribed as "k v cache"), speaker labels primarily correct but may shift in a few segments.
